content_text_body:
### Why is it important?

Effective action planning can be a complicated process. The Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) developed an action tool for use after organizations administer safety culture surveys and have analyzed their results. The action planning tool provides a number of steps to aid organizations in developing their own action plans to address patient safety and improve their safety culture, and can be used as a starting point. **Below are a few steps AHRQ recommends for effective action response to patient safety feedback:**

- **Secure Leadership Support**  
According to AHRQ, "Strong leadership commitment at all levels is essential to the success of an initiative and may need to be your first step in the action planning process. A good strategy is to seek leadership support before starting action planning and to confirm that support again during and after action plan development." Further, it is important to gain the support of managers, as well as supervisors whose assistance will be needed in the creation or execution of the action plan. 

- **Form an Action Planning Team**  
Strategically forming an action planning team can also help ensure the plan you put together is high quality and effective. AHRQ recommends that leaders keep in mind the following considerations when choosing members of the action planning team:

>- Make the team multidisciplinary, with a variety of roles, expertise, skills, and perspectives. Some important skills for members might include data analysis, quality improvement, human resources, or project management. 
>- You may already have an existing committee or group whose members can serve as the core of your action planning team. 
>- Remember to include clinicians!
>- Ask a senior leader to join the team and lend support in a visible and ongoing way. This is a great way to engage such leaders in the process and ensure their input and buy-in.
>- Include team members whose work will be directly affected by the planned initiatives. They will bring an important stakeholder perspective to the development and implementation of the action plan. 
>- Add new team members as needed.

- **Develop Your Action Plan - Answer 10 Key Questions**  
After you've completed the first two steps, you're ready to take action. The following questions can be helpful in developing your plan as you move forward.  
>Defining your goals and selecting your initiatives: 
>- What areas do you want to focus on for improvement? 
>- What are your goals? 
>- What initiatives will you implement? 

>Planning your initiatives: 
>- Who will be affected, and how? 
>- Who can lead the initiative? 
>- What resources will be needed? 
>- What are possible barriers, and how can they be overcome? 
>- How will you measure progress and success? 
>- What is the timeline? 

>Communicating your action plan: 
>- How will you share your action plan and with whom?

For additional information on effective action planning, refer to the [full article](https://www.ahrq.gov/sites/default/files/wysiwyg/professionals/quality-patient-safety/patientsafetyculture/planningtool.pdf).

>Source:

>Sorra J, Gray L, Franklin M, et al. Action Planning Tool for the AHRQ Surveys on Patient Safety Culture. (Prepared by Westat, Rockville, MD, under Contract No. HHSA 290201300003C). Rockville, MD: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality; January 2016. AHRQ Publication No. 16-0008-EF.
